raw_case_text:
A 57-year-old Indian male with HIV-positive status was admitted to our hospital with chief complaints of large-volume watery stools without blood or mucus, 3-4 times a day for 4 months with recent exacerbation for 1 week. This was also associated with nausea, loss of appetite, significant weight loss, generalized weakness, and dysphagia to solids. He denied personal or family history of allergies. He was diagnosed with HIV infection 17 years ago and was on treatment with antiretroviral drugs, namely raltegravir, lamivudine, and efavirenz. He was also diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis 5 months back for which he was on treatment with isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. He unintentionally lost 20 kg of weight over the past 4 months. He further denied the use of laxatives or any complementary or alternative medications. He had stable vital signs, was cachectic, and had a normal systemic examination. His workup for chronic diarrhea included a normal thyroid function test and no opportunistic infections or helminthic infestation. Stool analysis including culture was negative for Clostridium difficile toxin, Cryptosporidium, Vibrio cholerae, acid-fast bacteria, or any other parasites. Serum IgE concentration was also within the normal range. Other investigations revealed hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL (13-18 g/dL), platelets 244,000/uL (140,000-440,000/uL), and total leukocyte count 4880/mm3 (4000-10000/mm3) with neutrophils 78.5% (40%-75%), lymphocytes 16.2% (20%-45%), and eosinophils 0.8% (1%-6%). His total protein was 5.4 g/dL (6.60-8.70 g/dL), albumin 1.8 g/dL (3.97-4.94 g/dL), absolute CD4 count 89.91/mm3 of blood (400-1600/mm3 of blood), absolute CD8 count 427.68/mm3 of blood (280-1400/mm3 of blood), CD4 (helper T-cells)% 11.1% (28-58%), CD8 (suppressor T-cells)% 52.8% (19-49%), CD4/CD8 0.21 (1.2-3.3), and HIV-1 viral load by TaqMan plasma (quantitative) 12,59,309 copies/mL.
On further investigations, esophagogastro duodenoscopy revealed white mucosal plaques in the esophagus consistent with esophageal candidiasis. The mucosa of the duodenum showed focal erosions with blunting of the villi as seen in Figure 1. Urease test was negative for Helicobacter pylori. Mucosal biopsies from the stomach and duodenum were taken. Histopathology study shown in Figure 2 revealed active inflammation in the gastric and duodenal mucosa with excess eosinophils (20 eosinophils/high-power field) and no microorganisms. This was consistent with EGE. He also had a colonoscopy which was normal. Rifampicin was stopped during this admission for a period of 2 weeks. However, the persistence of diarrhea ruled out drug-induced EGE. He was then started on oral prednisolone 40 mg once daily. The frequency of stools decreased and consistency improved. Prednisolone was gradually tapered over a period of 2 months. This was associated with an increase in the frequency of watery stools like before resulting in a readmission with dehydration and weight loss.
The patient was restarted on oral prednisolone 60 mg once daily. Along with cessation of diarrhea, his appetite and weight improved during follow-up after 30 days. On 6-month follow-up, he has regained 18 kg and has normal stools. He is currently on oral prednisolone 40 mg once daily.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 57-year-old HIV-positive Indian male on anti-tuberculosis and antiretroviral therapy presented with a 4-month history of large-volume non-bloody watery diarrhea (3–4 episodes/day, worsening over the past week), a 20 kg weight loss, anorexia, nausea, generalized weakness, and solid-food dysphagia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 4 months preceding admission—shortly after starting quadruple anti-tuberculosis therapy 5 months earlier for pulmonary tuberculosis—the patient experienced persistent large-volume watery diarrhea without blood or mucus (3–4 stools daily, acutely worsening 1 week prior to admission), accompanied by nausea, anorexia, a 20 kg unintentional weight loss, profound weakness, and dysphagia to solids.
subjective.past_medical_history: 17-year history of HIV-1 infection on antiretroviral therapy; pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosed 5 months prior and treated with first-line anti-tubercular therapy. Denied personal or family history of atopic/allergic disorders or laxative/herbal use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic watery diarrhea, 20 kg weight loss over 4 months, anorexia, nausea, weakness, and solid-food dysphagia; negative for hematochezia or melena. Home medications: raltegravir, lamivudine, efavirenz, isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol.

objective.physical_examination: Cachectic appearance with stable vital signs and an otherwise unremarkable systemic physical examination.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL [normal 13–18]), platelets 244,000/µL, WBC 4,880/mm3 (78.5% neutrophils, 16.2% lymphocytes, 0.8% eosinophils), hypoproteinemia (total protein 5.4 g/dL [normal 6.60–8.70]), severe hypoalbuminemia (albumin 1.8 g/dL [normal 3.97–4.94]), and normal thyroid function and serum IgE levels. Stool cultures, Clostridium difficile toxin, Cryptosporidium, Vibrio cholerae, AFB stains, and ova/parasite exams were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: T-lymphocyte subset analysis revealed severe immunosuppression: absolute CD4+ count 89.91 cells/mm3 (11.1%; normal 400–1,600), absolute CD8+ count 427.68 cells/mm3 (52.8%), and CD4/CD8 ratio 0.21. Colonoscopy was normal. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) revealed white esophageal plaques consistent with esophageal candidiasis and focal duodenal mucosal erosions with villous blunting (rapid urease test negative for Helicobacter pylori). Gastric and duodenal mucosal biopsies demonstrated active gastroduodenitis with dense mucosal eosinophilic infiltration (20 eosinophils/HPF) and no opportunistic microorganisms, diagnostic of eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EGE).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Primary mucosal eosinophilic gastroenteritis (EGE, confirmed by gastroduodenal biopsies showing >=20 eosinophils/HPF without peripheral eosinophilia or elevated IgE after comprehensive exclusion of enteric opportunistic parasites/bacteria and a 2-week rifampicin dechallenge) and concurrent esophageal candidiasis in a 57-year-old male with advanced virologically failing HIV-1 infection (plasma HIV-1 RNA 1,259,309 copies/mL by TaqMan PCR, CD4+ count 89.91 cells/mm3, CD4/CD8 ratio 0.21) and pulmonary tuberculosis. Oral prednisolone (40 mg daily) rapidly controlled his diarrhea, and after a diarrheal relapse during a 2-month steroid taper, re-initiation of oral prednisolone (60 mg daily tapered to 40 mg daily maintenance) achieved complete remission of diarrhea and an 18 kg weight gain at 6-month follow-up.
